question: What CTopBar writes into each of its elements - which figure, in what format, in which colour - and which buttons it wires, for the rewrite's first screen.

addresses.name: CTopBar::Update
addresses.comment: **Slot 4 of CTopBar: fills the bar.** Bare `ret` at 0x6CB918. For the played country (idler slot 23 for the tag) it sets, each through the window's slot 14 by name and GuiObject_textBoxType::SetText: the seven resources by CTopBar::FormatGoodsNumber - energy 5, metal 4, raremat 6, oil 3, fuel 1, supplies 0, money 2, with fuel and supplies replaced by '-' for a government in exile; `ic_number` as `{colour}wasted/{colour}used/before-cap` from GetAvailableIC, +0x604 and +0x60C, red when wasted > 0 and when +0x60C > +0x604; `DateText` from the literal 'h :00 w d , w mw w y', only when the tick has changed; `dissent_number` coloured by the sign of GetDissentChange, one decimal above 1.000 and two below; `national_unity_number` coloured by the sign of the three strat impacts plus modifier 44, no decimals and a '%'; `diplomacy_number` as the integer part of +0xA88, or 100 when the global at 0x1BEA410 is set - **its colour is computed and appended to the string national unity has already used, so it is never shown**; `manpower_number` from +0xBCC with no decimals; `leadership_number` as **the officer ratio** (+0xD4) times 100 with a '%', red under 500 and yellow under 900; `espionage_number` as spy_pool over 1000, '99+' above 99. Then the flag and CountryName when the country changed, and `speed_indicator`'s frame: 1 when paused, game_speed + 2 otherwise. With a scenario at game state +0xD0C it disables seven of the main buttons.
addresses.evidence: Read through from 0x6C9FA0. Element names are pushed literals: 0x6CA017 'energy_number', 0x6CA932 'ic_number', 0x6CAA91 'DateText', 0x6CAC41 'dissent_number', 0x6CADE9 'national_unity_number', 0x6CAFAA 'diplomacy_number', 0x6CB00D 'manpower_number', 0x6CB16E 'leadership_number', 0x6CB3D1 'espionage_number', 0x6CB5A0 'speed_indicator'. The lost colour: `lea ecx,[esp+0xc0]; call appendChars` at 0x6CAF2B under two pushes is the esp+0xB8 the unity text was set from at 0x6CAE22, while the number is appended at esp+0x12C and SetText takes `lea edi,[esp+0x12c]` at 0x6CAFE3. The live strings of FINDINGS-guilive.md section 6 fit every format: '\xa7R10/\xa7G21/21', '\xa7G108%', '\xa7Y80%', '\xa7G0.00', '9', '115', '0'. What would show it wrong: a top bar whose diplomacy figure is coloured.

addresses.name: CTopBar::Build
addresses.comment: **Slot 0 of CTopBar: makes the window and wires its buttons.** Bare `ret` at 0x6CCB72. Creates the window 'topbar' through the gui and keeps it at +0x20; finds each button by name with the window's slot 13 and attaches an observer to its observable half at +0x48 (slot 1; slot 2 detaches): diplo +0x34, prod +0x60, tech +0x8C, politics +0xB8, intelligence +0xE4 - those five only while no tutorial runs - theatre +0x110, menubutton +0x13C, statistics +0x270, swm_open +0x29C, speeddown +0x2C8, speedup +0x320, outlinerbutton +0x34C, and **one observer at +0x2F4 for both `speed_indicator` and `pause_bg`**. Rebuilds the object at +0x378, makes the one at +0x380 if absent, sets `pause_bg` to frame 1 with the tooltip PAUSE_RESUME when paused and frame 2 with FE_PAUSED_TEXT when not. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Pushed literals in order: 0x6CBC1D 'topbar', 0x6CBC95 'topbarbutton_diplo', 0x6CBD03 'topbarbutton_prod', 0x6CBD86 'topbarbutton_tech', 0x6CBDF7 'topbarbutton_politics', 0x6CBE5F 'topbarbutton_intelligence', 0x6CC0CF 'topbar_menubutton', 0x6CC136 'topbarbutton_statistics', 0x6CC19C 'topbarbutton_theatre', 0x6CC202 'swm_open', 0x6CC367 'speed_indicator', 0x6CC3CA 'pause_bg', 0x6CC44B 'button_speedup', 0x6CC4AA 'button_speeddown', 0x6CC616 'topbar_outlinerbutton'. `lea eax,[esi+0x2f4]` at both 0x6CC39D and 0x6CC404. `push 1`/`push 2` before slot 18 at 0x6CC853 and 0x6CC9C8. What would show it wrong: a second observer for pause_bg written by the constructor.

addresses.name: CTopBar::Show
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CTopBar, thirty bytes: when there is a window at +0x20, calls slot 13 of its CGuiObject subobject at +0x18 - Show, the neighbour of the Hide that CFixedWindow::Hide calls on children at slot 14 - and then CTopBar::SyncOutliner.
addresses.evidence: `cmp dword ptr [edi+0x20],0; je; mov ecx,[edi+0x20]; mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; mov edx,[eax+0x34]; add ecx,0x18; call edx; call 0x6cb920; ret` at 0x6C9C93..0x6C9CAD.

addresses.name: CTopBar::FormatGoodsNumber
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __stdcall CTopBar::FormatGoodsNumber(int goods@ECX, CTopBar* topBar@stack:4, Hoi3CString* out@stack:8) @EAX
addresses.comment: **One resource of the top bar as text: a colour escape and the stockpile.** `ret 8`, goods in ECX. out = sent_to - repaid_away - tribute_sent + usage + conversion_used + convoyed_out + traded_away; in = home_produced (+ convoyed_in unless goods is 0 or 1) + sent_back + the pool at +0xA64 + income_from_debt + conversion_made + tribute_received. **Red when out > in + traded_for, green when out < CCountry::GetDailyIncome, yellow otherwise.** The number is the country's stockpile - pool_in_exile for a government in exile, else the acting capital's pool at +0x15C - through FormatFixedPoint with no decimals; above 99999000 it is divided by a thousand first and given a 'K'.
addresses.evidence: `mov edi,ecx` at 0x6C9CE0 and `mov ecx,5` before the call at 0x6CA03F. The fifteen arrays are read at 0x6C9D08..0x6C9D77 as [country + goods*4 + N]. `cmp eax,edx; jle` at 0x6C9D80 pushes 0x15B5C58 (a7 52, red) on the taken side; `cmp ebx,[eax]; jge` after GetDailyIncome at 0x6C9DC0 chooses 0x15B5C50 (a7 47, green) or 0x15B5C54 (a7 59, yellow). `cmp dword ptr [eax+edi*4+8],0x5f5dd18` at 0x6C9DF7; 0x15C7718 is 'K'. What would show it wrong: a stockpile over 99999 drawn without a K.

addresses.name: CTopBar::SyncOutliner
addresses.comment: Called at the end of CTopBar::Show and from CTopBar::Update. The top bar arrives in EDI. With an object at +0x378 it asks it a yes/no (0x6A7D60), consults what the idler holds at +0xCFC/+0xD00 and +0x1CE0, and shows or hides `topbar_outlinerbutton`, setting and clearing the byte at +0x37C around 0x6CFEA0. **Likely** keeps the outliner button in step with whether the outliner may be shown; the callees were not read and the name is a guess at that.
addresses.evidence: `mov ecx,[edi+0x378]` at 0x6CB938 with no load of EDI before it; 'topbar_outlinerbutton' pushed at 0x6CB993, 0x6CBA53 and 0x6CBAA8; `mov byte ptr [edi+0x37c],1` at 0x6CBA4A and `,bl` at 0x6CBB3F. What would settle it: reading 0x6A7D60 and 0x6CFEA0.

addresses.name: CTopBar::CTopBar
addresses.no_signature: the argument list was not read; the caller pushes after the allocation and the body was not decoded
addresses.comment: The constructor: writes the vftable 0x15D2C90 at 0x6C95D4. One caller, 0x65D727, after `push 0x384; call operator new` at 0x65D705 - so a CTopBar is 0x384 bytes. Not read beyond that; it is where the thirteen button observers of CTopBar::Build get their handlers.
addresses.evidence: image.findValue(0x15D2C90) answers 0x6C95D4 and 0x6C9B7F, and functionStart(0x6C95D4) is 0x6C9530. The bytes before the call are `68 84 03 00 00 e8 ...`.

addresses.name: ParseGuiOrientation
addresses.comment: **The `orientation` keyword of a .gui element as a number**, compared exactly and case-sensitively: UPPER_LEFT 0, UPPER_RIGHT 1, LOWER_LEFT 2, LOWER_RIGHT 3, CENTER 4, CENTER_UP 5, CENTER_DOWN 6, and **anything else 0** - a misspelt orientation is silently the upper left. The string arrives in EDI; bare `ret`s. CWindowType::LoadKey's `orientation` case calls it. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Seven compares against 0x1602128, 0x1602134, 0x1602140, 0x160214C, 0x1602158, 0x1602160 and 0x160216C, the first two inline byte loops and the rest through 0x40C3C0; the last ends `movzx eax,al; neg eax; sbb eax,eax; and eax,6` at 0x00B29DA8. What would show it wrong: a caller lowering the case first.

addresses.name: GuiObject_textBoxType::SetText
addresses.comment: **Sets a text box's text.** The box in ESI, the string in EDI. Compares the string with the one at +0xD8 (0x4173C0) and returns when they are equal; otherwise assigns it and has the object at +0x4C lay it out again (slot 61), handing it the string, the font name at +0x70, the string at +0x8C, the words at +0xA8 and +0xAA and the fields at +0xAC, +0xB0, +0xC4 and +0xC8. What CTopBar::Update sets every figure through. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: `mov eax,edi; lea edx,[esi+0xd8]; call 0x4173c0; test al,al; jne` at 0x00A87F38, then `push -1; push 0; push edi; lea ecx,[esi+0xd8]; call std::string::assignString` at 0x00A87F49. What would show it wrong: a text box whose +0xD8 changes without this running.

addresses.name: IntToString
addresses.comment: A plain int as decimal text: constructs the out string empty, `_itoa`s the value in ECX in radix 10 into a stack buffer and assigns it. `ret 4`. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: `mov esi,[ebp+8]`, the three stores of an empty string, `push 0xa; lea eax,[ebp-0x2c]; push eax; push ecx; call 0xb9a0c4` at 0x00A5AB71..0x00A5AB7F, then the strlen loop and std::string::assign.

addresses.name: std::string::constructCString
addresses.comment: `std::basic_string<char>::basic_string(const char*)` with the ordinary convention: `this` in ECX, the C string on the stack, `ret 4`, returns `this`. The register-argument copy of the same constructor is std::string::fromCString.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x432230..0x432267: the empty-string stores, a strlen loop, `push eax; push edx; mov ecx,esi; call std::string::assign; mov eax,esi; ret 4`.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetDiploInfluence
addresses.comment: Diplomatic influence as callers are meant to read it: **100000 when the global at 0x1BEA410 is set**, +0xA88 otherwise. `ret 4`. CTopBar::Update makes the same test inline before drawing the figure.
addresses.evidence: `cmp dword ptr [0x1bea410],0; mov eax,[ebp+8]; je; mov dword ptr [eax],0x186a0; pop ebp; ret 4` at 0x4F4E23..0x4F4E36, and `mov ecx,[ecx+0xa88]` at 0x4F4E39.

addresses.name: g_UnlimitedDiploInfluence
addresses.comment: A dword that, when not zero, makes every reader of a country's diplomatic influence see 100. Tested in CCountry::GetDiploInfluence, in CTopBar::Update at 0x6CAF37 and at 26 other sites, most between 0xA15000 and 0xA34000. **What sets it was not found, and the name is a guess at its purpose.**
addresses.evidence: image.findValue(0x1BEA410) answers 28 sites; the two read are `cmp dword ptr [0x1bea410],0` at 0x4F4E23 and `cmp dword ptr [0x1bea410],ebx` at 0x6CAF37, each followed by a store or load of 0x186A0. What would settle it: the one site among the 28 that writes.

structs.name: CTopBar
structs.comment: The bar across the top of the in-game screen. Six virtual slots: 0 Build, 1 the destructor, 2 Show, 3 a shared body, 4 Update, 5 BuildTooltip.
structs.evidence: The RTTI export gives CTopBar one vftable at 0x15D2C90 with six slots; `push 0x384; call operator new` at 0x65D705 before the constructor call at 0x65D727. What would show the size wrong: a member written past +0x380.

struct_fields.name: window
struct_fields.comment: The live `topbar` window. Every element is found through it: slot 13 a button by name, slot 14 a text box, slot 17 an icon.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov [esi+0x20],eax` at 0x6CBC81 after the by-name window factory is called with 'topbar'.

struct_fields.name: idler
struct_fields.comment: The in-game screen. Slot 14 gives the gui, slot 23 the played country's tag, slot 95 whether the game is paused.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov ecx,[esi+0x24]; mov eax,[ecx]; mov edx,[eax+0x38]; call edx` at 0x6CBC3E; `mov edx,[eax+0x17c]` at 0x6CC806 and 0x6CB58C.

struct_fields.name: shown_tick
struct_fields.comment: The tick `DateText` was last drawn for; the date is redrawn only when the game state's tick differs.
struct_fields.evidence: `cmp edi,[ecx+0x28]; je` at 0x6CAA06 with edi = game state +0xBDC, and `mov [esi+0x28],edi` at 0x6CAAA6.

struct_fields.name: shown_player
struct_fields.comment: The country the flag and the name were last drawn for: the tag, then at +0x30 the id that is compared.
struct_fields.evidence: `cmp [edi+0x30],eax; je` at 0x6CB43D; `mov [esi+0x2c],ecx` and `mov [esi+0x30],edx` at 0x6CB533 and 0x6CB539.

A button's frame number is one-based on the evidence of three uses: speed_indicator 1..6 against noOfFrames = 6, pause_bg 1..2 against 2, the outliner button 1..2.
